subject: Clearsail: EU edge 502/503 + APAC failover causing retry amplification
messages:
From: Alice Ramos <alice@clearsail.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: support@clearsail.com
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: EU edge 502/503 spike, APAC fallback amplifying retries

Jonas —

We just observed a sustained spike of 502/503 responses originating in eu-west ingress starting ~08:50PST (15:50 UTC). Some of our customers are seeing timeouts and client retries; traffic is being routed to APAC as a fallback which looks like it's triggering an amplification loop (clients retry faster than the backends are able to recover).

Observed: 
- ~18% 502/503 rate on eu-west LB over the past 20m
- APAC ingress showing a 3x traffic increase and elevated 429s
- Some request traces show repeated retries with identical x-request-id headers being processed multiple times

I've attached a small snapshot and the health-check logs. We're paging the Clearsail SRE oncall now. Can Redwood advise whether there are any recent LB config rollouts or routing changes? We need an immediate workaround and then root cause.

Attachments: clearsail_502_snapshot.png, edge_health_checks.log

Thanks,
Alice Ramos
Senior SRE — Clearsail

Subject: Fwd: Urgent: EU edge 502/503 spike, APAC fallback amplifying retries

Folks — forwarding Clearsail alert. Quick plan (15 min tactical):
1) Confirm whether there was any recent ingress LB rollout in eu-west in last 2 hours.
2) Temporarily shift Clearsail traffic away from eu-west to a dedicated pool with strict rate limiting (avoid automatic APAC fallback).
3) Increase LB instance count in eu-west and disable the header-rewrite rule that Alice mentioned previously (suspected mismatch).
4) Ask Clearsail to enable client-side retry jitter or extended backoff (short-term).

Marissa — please take point on the LB change. Vivek — I might need you to sign off on a temporary credit/expedite with Cleansail (exec note). Laura — I'll need a postmortem template and customer-facing note if we have to offer credits.

I'll update the thread as we confirm steps.

— Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: EU edge 502/503 spike, APAC fallback amplifying retries

On Thu, May 9, 2029 at 9:18 AM jonas.weber@redwood.ai wrote:
> Folks — forwarding Clearsail alert. Quick plan (15 min tactical):

Confirmed: there was a canary LB config rollout at 08:40PST that included a new header-rewrite (strip x-forwarded-proto) and a healthcheck tweak. Early signs: health checks to one backend pool are returning 502 intermittently because the rewrite removed a required header the backend expects. That explains eu-west 502s -> traffic then moving east.

Tactical actions executed (09:25):
- Disabled header-rewrite rule on eu-west canary (rolled back to previous config).
- Scaled eu-west ingress pool +30% capacity (auto-scale kicked, I added one extra instance).
- Toggled routing policy for Clearsail to prefer a dedicated eu pool (no automatic cross-region failover) until we verify.

Immediate observable impact: eu-west 502 rate dropped from 18% to ~3% in the first 5 minutes; APAC traffic reduced ~40% from peak. We're still monitoring traces for duplicate x-request-id replays.

Follow-up: I'll open SUP-4891 with the rollback diff and logs. We should schedule a config audit to prevent header-dependent health checks.

Marissa Cole
Sr. SRE, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: alice@clearsail.com, ops@clearsail.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RESOLVED: Clearsail EU edge incident — rollback applied, monitoring continued

Alice / Clearsail Ops —

Summary:
- Root cause: canary LB rollout removed a required header which caused intermittent backend 502s; that triggered cross-region failover and retry amplification.
- Mitigation applied: header-rewrite was rolled back (09:25), eu-west pool scaled +30% (09:25–09:30), Clearsail routing temporarily pinned to dedicated eu pool.
- Outcome: 502/503 rate back to baseline (~<1%) by 09:35 PST; APAC load returned to normal levels and 429s reduced. No additional customer-facing escalations reported after the mitigation window.

Next steps:
1) SUP-4891 opened with rollout diff and logs (Marissa).
2) Config audit for header-dependent health checks and stricter canary guardrails (owner: Marissa, due 2029-05-16).
3) Customer comms: Laura to send a short note and propose modest credits if Clearsail reports any downstream customer retention issues.

Thanks to the oncall and Clearsail SRE for quick coordination. I'm keeping the ticket open for 24 hours for observation.

— Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
